title: Using an Angular Decorator like @Output with a string literal class member causes a build error

labels.name: regression
labels.description: Indicates than the issue relates to something that worked in a previous version

labels.name: area: compiler

milestone.title: needsTriage

body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by package @angular/compiler-cli@10.0.6 ### Is this a regression? Yes, the previous version in which this bug was not present was: @angular/compiler-cli@10.0.5 ### Description I think this is related to the feature added in PR https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/38226 I had some code like this before: ``` @Output() 'did-finish-load' = new EventEmitter(); ``` (`did-finish-load` is the name of an [Electron API](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/api/web-contents#event-did-finish-load) I was using, I was just trying to keep the same naming scheme). It looks like before, output names like `'did-finish-load'` were just ignored completely. In the newer Angular version, it causes a mysterious build error. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction I don't think I can control the compiler-cli version on StackBlitz, so I'll submit a github repo. https://github.com/patdx/reproduction-string-literal-angular Steps: 1. npm install 2. ng build 3. You should get the same error as reported below ## 🔥 Exception or Error I just tried creating a small test: ``` export class AppComponent { @Output() 'did-finish-load-one' = new EventEmitter(); @Output() didFinishLoadTwo = new EventEmitter(); } ``` With `@angular/compiler-cli@10.0.5`, it produced the following code in dist/main.js: ``` class AppComponent { constructor() { this[ "did-finish-load-one" ] = new _angular_core__WEBPACK_IMPORTED_MODULE_0__["EventEmitter"](); this.didFinishLoadTwo = new _angular_core__WEBPACK_IMPORTED_MODULE_0__[ "EventEmitter" ](); } } AppComponent.ɵfac = function AppComponent_Factory(t) { return new (t || AppComponent)(); }; AppComponent.ɵcmp = _angular_core__WEBPACK_IMPORTED_MODULE_0__[ "ɵɵdefineComponent" ]({ type: AppComponent, selectors: [["app-root"]], outputs: { didFinishLoadTwo: "didFinishLoadTwo" }, decls: 0, vars: 0, template: function AppComponent_Template(rf, ctx) {}, encapsulation: 2, }); /*@__PURE__*/ (function () { _angular_core__WEBPACK_IMPORTED_MODULE_0__["ɵsetClassMetadata"]( AppComponent, [ { type: _angular_core__WEBPACK_IMPORTED_MODULE_0__["Component"], args: [ { selector: "app-root", template: "", }, ], }, ], null, { didFinishLoadTwo: [ { type: _angular_core__WEBPACK_IMPORTED_MODULE_0__["Output"], }, ], } ); })(); ``` This code is running, but "did-finish-load-one" was totally ignored as an output. Oh! Actually, I didn't realize this before. With `@angular/compiler-cli@10.0.6`, I got a build error instead: ```bash # ... chunk {styles} styles.js, styles.js.map (styles) 12.4 kB [initial] [rendered] chunk {vendor} vendor.js, vendor.js.map (vendor) 2.07 MB [initial] [rendered] Date: 2020-07-31T04:45:05.022Z - Hash: ad1181a1bd231bc94cd9 - Time: 5662ms ERROR in ./src/app/app.component.ts 17:19 Module parse failed: Unexpected token (17:19) File was processed with these loaders: * ./node_modules/@ngtools/webpack/src/index.js You may need an additional loader to handle the result of these loaders. | template: '', | }] > }], null, { did-finish-load-one: [{ | type: Output | }], didFinishLoadTwo: [{ ``` It guess if the compiler supports string literals with decorators like Output, it needs to escape the value here, as in ```diff template: '', }] - }], null, { did-finish-load-one: [{ + }], null, { 'did-finish-load-one': [{ type: Output }], didFinishLoadTwo: [{ ``` ## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 

Angular CLI: 10.0.4
Node: 12.3.1
OS: win32 x64

Angular: 10.0.7
... animations, common, compiler, core, forms, platform-browser
... platform-browser-dynamic, router
Ivy Workspace: Yes
**Anything else relevant?** As far as I can tell, all that matters is `@angular/compiler-cli@10.0.5` (ignored but no error) vs `@angular/compiler-cli@10.0.6` (build error).
